content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-maths-subtraction","title":"Subtraction with Borrowing","quick":"When the ones digit on top is smaller than the ones digit below, borrow 10 from the tens place. Then subtract normally.","full":"Think of a kirana shop. You have 4 ten-rupee notes and 5 one-rupee coins (45 rupees), and you must pay 18 rupees. You need to give 8 ones but you only have 5 ones, so you break one ten-rupee note into 10 coins. Now you have 3 tens and 15 ones. Subtract ones: 15-8=7. Subtract tens: 3-1=2. Answer is 27 rupees left. The key idea: borrowing just renames one ten as ten ones, it does not change the total value, only how it is grouped.","tip":"Borrow means break one ten into ten ones, nothing is lost, just rearranged.","answer":"27","traps":["Subtracting the smaller digit from the larger digit regardless of position, ignoring borrowing","Forgetting to reduce the tens digit by 1 after borrowing","Writing the ones answer but forgetting to carry the borrow correctly in tens"],"misconception":"Child thinks you can always subtract bottom digit from top digit without caring which is bigger, so they flip 8-5 instead of borrowing.","parent_questions":[{"q":"Why do we borrow 10 from the tens place here?","expected_answer_hint":"Because 5 ones is less than 8 ones, we need more ones, so we break one ten into 10 ones."},{"q":"After borrowing, how many tens and ones does 45 become?","expected_answer_hint":"3 tens and 15 ones."}],"check_question":{"q":"52 − 27 = ____","options":["25","35","15"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! You borrowed a ten to make 12-7=5, then 4-2=2, giving 25.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. Borrow a ten: 12-7=5, then 4-2=2, so answer is 25."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A child paying a shopkeeper with rupee notes and coins at a small kirana shop counter.","labels":[{"text":"tens","position":"left"},{"text":"ones","position":"right"}]}}
